Playbook.name: O365 — Password Spraying: One Source Failing Against Many Accounts - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source IP failed logins against >=8 distinct O365 accounts in the window, excluding the egress NAT - cloud password spraying. Triage: real spray from attacker infrastructure, or residual NAT/proxy noise?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A successful cloud spray yields a valid identity that bypasses on-prem controls.

Assets.AssetType: Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, Teams, Entra directory

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: O365 unified audit via Elastic Agent (verified live). Fields: event.action, user.name, source.ip, o365.audit.Operation, o365.audit.ResultStatus, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.ModifiedProperties, o365.audit.Parameters, o365.audit.UserId. INGEST LAG 20-60 min - all queries use a 4h window and timestamp_override event.ingested at rule level.
JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24 - internal users appear from it.

Signal.Name: Password Spraying: One Source Failing Ag
Signal.Details: source.ip failing >=8 distinct accounts (egress NAT excluded).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the source sprayed cloud accounts and whether any login succeeded.

Step.name: Sprayed accounts and errors
Step.Purpose: Many distinct accounts each failing a few times is the spray signature.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND event.action == "UserLoginFailed" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS fails = COUNT(*), users = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.name), user_list = VALUES(user.name), errors = VALUES(o365.audit.LogonError) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: 8+ distinct users with low per-user fails and InvalidUserNameOrPassword = spray. The source being foreign (not 94.249.88.x) confirms external attack infrastructure.

Step.name: Any success from the spraying source
Step.Purpose: A success for any sprayed account is compromise.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND event.action == "UserLoggedIn" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logins = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(user.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Any success = escalate to compromise and reset that account.

Node.Condition: A success from the spraying source for a sprayed account.
8+ distinct accounts sprayed from an external source, no success.
Source resolves to the egress NAT or a known proxy (should be excluded).

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-O365SPRAY-USERS, INV-02-O365SPRAY-SUCCESS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Egress NAT / proxy aggregating internal failures.

SOCAction.Item: Block the source; reset any compromised account + tokens; enforce CA/MFA.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A broken SSO/federation client failing many accounts.

Indicators.Item: One client failing federation for many users.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the change/actor in the audit log.
If unexpected/unauthorised, disable the actor session and reverse the change.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reverse the change; revoke sessions/tokens for the actor and affected principals.
Review the actor's other recent audit activity.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce MFA/conditional access; tighten admin consent and privileged-role governance (PIM); alert on these operations.

QualityChecks.Check: Account for O365 ingest lag (20-60 min) - short windows miss events; this rule uses event.ingested override.
Exclude the egress NAT 94.249.88.0/24 where source is used; tune known admin/automation via exceptions.
